lines.text: Ben-hadad king of Aram besieged Samaria, and the famine grew so bad that a donkey's head sold for eighty shekels of silver.
The king tore his clothes, then swore that the head of Elisha son of Shaphat would not stay on his shoulders.
Four men with leprosy decided to go to the camp of the Moabites, and they set out at twilight.
The scouts took two chariots with horses and followed the Arameans as far as the Euphrates, finding clothing and equipment strewn along the way.
The people plundered the Aramean camp, flour and barley sold for a shekel, and the people trampled the officer in the gateway.
